title: More stormy weather forecast for B.C. with warnings for flooding, heavy rain, fog
summary: As rain persists on Vancouver Island, fog advisories have been issued for the Cariboo, East Kootenay, Prince George, Similkameen and South Okanagan regions on Friday.

image.caption: Rain is expected to continue through the weekend on Vancouver Island, according to Environment Canada. (Ben Nelms/CBC)

blocks.text: As rain persists on Vancouver Island, fog advisories have been issued for the Cariboo, East Kootenay, Prince George, Similkameen and South Okanagan regions on Friday.
Pemberton Valley remains under shelter-in-place advisory, with evacuation orders for some parts
Flood watches and warnings, rainfall warnings and fog advisories are in effect for much of B.C. as a series of storms moves through the province.

The entire South Coast, including Vancouver Island, is under a flood watch or warning on Friday morning. Areas of particular concern include the North Shore-Sea-to-Sky and Lower Fraser regions, as well as the Kingcome River area on the Central Coast, following a long period of heavy rain earlier this week.
B.C.'s River Forecast Centre says water levels in those areas have or will exceed river banks and cause flooding.

Residents in the Pemberton Valley have been advised to evacuate or shelter in place, depending on where they are. On Thursday, the Líl̓wat Nation said sections of Lillooet Lake Road had six inches to one foot of water flowing over it.

Rainfall warnings remain in effect for much of Vancouver Island on Friday. Anywhere from 50 to 100 millimetres is forecast for the north, west and inland areas of the Island according to Environment Canada, though 120 millimetres could fall in some local areas.
Areas including Gold River, Tahsis and Zeballos, the latter of which was evacuated last week due to landslide, will likely get the most rain, Environment Canada says.

blocks.text: The downpour is expected to ease Friday afternoon, but the weather agency warns more rain is on the way this weekend.

Meanwhile, fog advisories have been issued for the Cariboo, East Kootenay, Prince George, Similkameen and South Okanagan regions on Friday. Environment Canada says dense fog is creating "near-zero visibility" in some areas.
It adds that travel in dense fog can become hazardous, and is warning drivers of dangerous road conditions.
The fog is expected to lift late Friday morning, according to Environment Canada.
